title: Sable and the Ghost
premise: Dominic Zhou, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve of a flight no one would claim, is summoned when Meridian Flight 447's records vanish mid-flight while the plane is still airborne. Following the erased trail, she discovers the airline's founder left a hidden ledger proving the company falsified maintenance records for decades — and that the flight was deliberately scrubbed to bury a witness aboard. Hunted by the airline's fixers and betrayed by her own mentor, Dominic must trade the ledger — the one secret worth killing for, and her only leverage for the truth about row twelve — to a border official at a shifting checkpoint, choosing truth over the belonging she's spent her life chasing. In the end, the ledger goes public, the airline falls, and Dominic finally claims the names of her family in the official record.
about_author: August Almeida is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reviewing accident reports before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where fog delays more flights than weather ever explains.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Dominic Zhou's POV. Opening on the anniversary vigil, we learn her family died in row twelve of a flight officially attributed to pilot error — an attribution she never believed. A call pulls her to a live case: Meridian 447's digital records have vanished while the plane is still in the air. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Erasure
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the airline's operations center, she finds the deletion was surgical — not a hack but an authorized purge using founder-level credentials no one living should possess. The plane lands safely, but the cockpit voice recorder is blank. Beat: the uncanny dread of a crime committed against a thing that hasn't crashed yet.

chapters.title: Passenger Manifest, Missing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, intercut with the fixer Wren's. The passenger list is scrubbed too, but Dominic recovers a fragment: seat 12A was occupied by Ilsa Voss, a retired maintenance auditor. The connection to her own family's row twelve is too precise to be coincidence. Beat: the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Knew
chapters.summary: Dominic tracks Ilsa Voss to a safehouse; Wren arrives first, and Ilsa is gone — but a copied ledger page remains, showing decades of falsified maintenance sign-offs, including the flight that killed Dominic's family. Beat: confirmation that her grief was manufactured by negligence, then covered up.

chapters.title: The Founder's Hand
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We learn the purge orders came from Elias Meridian — the founder, officially dead for nine years, alive and erasing his empire's sins. Wren, loyal to the company that raised her, begins to doubt when ordered to eliminate Dominic. Beat: loyalty cracking under weight.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic confronts her mentor, Halvard, who admits he helped bury the original row-twelve findings to protect his career — and that Ilsa was his informant. He gives her the ledger's location, then is killed before she can leave. Beat: betrayal, and the terrible cost of half-truths.

chapters.title: Fugitive on the Corridor
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Dominic, now framed for Halvard's murder, flees toward the border with the ledger. Wren pursues, increasingly convinced the company intends to erase them both. The checkpoint between jurisdictions shifts shifts at dawn — a narrow window. Beat: relentless chase, rising stakes.

chapters.title: Elias Meridian
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She reaches the founder's lakeside estate first. Elias offers her a trade: the ledger for the full, unredacted file on her family's flight — and a place in his rebuilt company, a belonging she has never had. Beat: temptation, and the seduction of finally being wanted.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Dawn
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the shifting checkpoint, Wren turns her gun on Elias instead of Dominic; Dominic chooses truth over the offered belonging, surrendering the ledger to the border official and broadcasting its contents before the window closes. Elias is taken; Wren defects with testimony. Beat: the trade that costs everything and buys the truth.

chapters.title: Names in the Record
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Weeks later, the official report is rewritten; row twelve's passengers are named, causes corrected. Dominic visits the graves with the corrected file, no longer an investigator of unattributed losses but a witness. Beat: quiet resolution — loyalty to the dead finally honored, belonging found in truth rather than offered.
